title: Annotatio V §.II Autoritative (Eph. 4): Keep the Spirit’s unity in the bond of peace — one body and one Spirit
pass_a_gloss: Autoritative from Ephesians chapter 4, to be reckoned as a quasi-common place of the thing to be proved, embracing besides the whole Foundation both Theoretical from v. 1 to 17 and Practical from v. 17 to the end of the chapter — when the Apostle in v. 3 bids keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace, and affirms one Body and Spirit, one Spiritual Body to be constituted, where there is one Lord, one faith, one Baptism, one God and Father of all, who is above all and through all and in all (vv. 4–6);
pass_b_english: By authority: take Ephesians 4 as a standing commonplace for the point — covering the whole foundation, theoretical (vv. 1–17) and practical (v. 17 to the chapter’s end).

There the Apostle bids us keep the Spirit’s unity in the bond of peace (v. 3), and affirms one body and one Spirit — one spiritual body — where there is one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, above all, through all, and in all (vv. 4–6).
source_text: Autoritative ex Cap. 4. ad Ephes., rei probandae Loco quasi Communi reputando, totum insuper Fundamentum tàm Theoreticum à v. 1. ad 17. quàm Practicum à v. 17. ad fin. Cap. complexo, quando Apostolus v. 3. jubet servare unitatem Spiritûs in vinculo pacis, & unum Corpus Spiritumque, unum Corpus Spirituale constitui affirmat, ubi unus est Dominus, una fides, unum Baptisma, unus Deus & Pater omnium, qui est super omnes & per omnes & in omnibus v. 4. 5. 6.;
